note: Schema: game/scripts/sim/FORKS.md. Seed forks written by the sim builder; data agents extend this file.

forks.title: The waiting period
forks.text: Egypt has moved armour into Sinai, expelled the UN force and closed the Straits of Tiran to Israeli shipping. Reservists are mobilised and the economy is idling. The cabinet must decide how long to wait for diplomacy before force.

options.label: Allow about two weeks for diplomacy, bring Dayan in as defence minister, then let the defence establishment decide the timing
options.advocate: Prime Minister Eshkol's cabinet

lasting.label: Diplomacy seen to be exhausted first
Reserves and a unity government in place
Weeks of mobilisation idle the economy
Nation united: every diplomatic avenue seen to be tried

options.note: The cabinet voted on 4 June to let the defence establishment decide the timing; the air strike came on 5 June (S200).

options.label: Strike at once, before Egypt completes its deployment
options.advocate: Chief of Staff Rabin and the General Staff (Rabin argued Israel could not afford to wait, S200)

lasting.label: Seen as having fired before diplomacy ran its course
Initiative kept; reserves back at work sooner
Doves and part of the public uneasy at the first shot

cite.quote: Time is not on our side. And in a week or two, or in three or four weeks, the situation will be worse.

options.label: Keep waiting for the US-British international flotilla to reopen the Straits
options.advocate: Foreign Minister Eban, seeking Western backing (S1024, S1026)

lasting.label: Israel seen to have exhausted the international route
Western trade, credit and arms ties nurtured
Western academic and research ties deepened
Egyptian forces left to complete their deployment
Public anxiety, then doubt about a hesitant leadership
Public lost confidence in a hesitant leadership
Weeks of dread dent confidence to stay

cite.quote: Your message and your remarks and assurances to Mr. Eban had an important influence on our decision to await developments for a further limited period

forks.title: What to do with the territories
forks.text: Israel holds Sinai, Gaza, the West Bank and the Golan. For the West Bank (home to roughly a million Palestinians) ministers differ: Yigal Allon proposes keeping a strategic belt and returning the populated hills, others want annexation or autonomy.

options.label: Keep the Jordan Valley, East Jerusalem and the Etzion bloc; leave the populated hills unannexed pending negotiations
options.advocate: Yigal Allon (the Allon Plan, 27 July 1967)

lasting.label: Jordan Valley farms and a united Jerusalem
A compromise most of the public could accept

options.note: The plan was never formally adopted but served as the informal guide to settlement in the Jordan Valley and the Etzion bloc (S1114, S225).

options.label: Keep all the territories permanently and settle them
options.advocate: Signatories of the 'Greater Land of Israel' advertisement of 22 September 1967: Alterman, Tabenkin, Agnon and others (S603)

lasting.label: Palestinians placed under permanent Israeli rule
A long, populated front to defend
Mountain aquifer and Jordan Valley wells brought under Israeli control

cite.quote: a large advertisement appeared in several Israeli daily newspapers, signed by leading intellectuals of the country, including the poet Natan Altermann, the ideologue of the kibbutz movement Moshe Tabenkin, and the writer S.Y. Agnon

options.label: Allon's first version: a Palestinian autonomous region linked to Israel
options.advocate: Yigal Allon (initial version, rejected by most ministers on 30 July 1967, S225)

lasting.label: A route to a negotiated outcome
Autonomous area bordering the Jordan Valley
Open academic and trade links with Europe and the region
A negotiated path eases the national debate
Aquifer shared with the autonomous area

cite.quote: When he placed the original "Allon plan" on the cabinet's table on July 27, 1967, he had proposed that a Palestinian autonomy be set up in the West Bank.

forks.title: Settlers in Hebron
forks.text: A group led by Rabbi Moshe Levinger held a Passover seder at the Park Hotel in Hebron and refused to leave. Legal advisers warn that civilian settlement in occupied territory breaches the Fourth Geneva Convention. About 38,000 Palestinians live in Hebron.

options.label: Move the group into a military compound and later build Kiryat Arba on the city's edge
options.advocate: Eshkol's government

lasting.label: Jewish return to Hebron welcomed by many
Hebron's Palestinians live beside a settlement

options.note: The group was moved to a military compound; Kiryat Arba was built in 1970-71 on land requisitioned 'for military purposes' (S1260, S280).

options.label: Remove the group and enforce the legal advice
options.advocate: Theodor Meron, Foreign Ministry legal counsel (S604)

lasting.label: Rule of law upheld, welcomed by the secular public

cite.quote: The legal counsel of the Foreign Ministry, Theodor Meron, was asked whether international law allowed settlement in the newly conquered land. In a memo marked "Top Secret," Mr. Meron wrote unequivocally, "My conclusion is that civilian settlement in the administered territories contravenes the explicit provisions of the Fourth Geneva Convention."

options.label: Allow permanent Jewish settlement inside Hebron itself
options.advocate: Rabbi Levinger's group (S1260)

lasting.label: Palestinian residents displaced from the centre
Settlement inside a Palestinian city condemned
Troops tied down guarding the enclave
A larger settler population in Hebron
Secular public alarmed at the enclave

cite.quote: Moshe Levinger even brought a refrigerator and a washing machine with him.

forks.title: Rogers Plan or deep strikes?
forks.text: The War of Attrition is bleeding the Bar-Lev line, and Egypt's canal cities are under fire. US Secretary of State Rogers has proposed a settlement plan; Israel can reject it and carry the air war deep into Egypt, accept it, or keep the fighting to the Canal zone.

options.label: Reject the Rogers Plan and bomb targets deep inside Egypt
options.advocate: Prime Minister Meir's government

lasting.label: Air force pressure on Egypt, a quieter canal
Strikes on Egyptian towns and factories criticised
Defence research and an air industry push

options.note: Israel rejected the plan for failing to secure agreed borders and struck deep in Egypt from early 1970; Soviet pilots flew over Egypt by April 1970 and a ceasefire came on 7-8 August 1970 (S1265).

options.label: Accept the Rogers Plan for an Israel-Egypt settlement
options.advocate: US Secretary of State Rogers (S1265)

lasting.label: Israel seen to engage with a US plan
Lower defence burden, trade and investment
Hawks angry; coalition split over the plan

cite.quote: On December 9, 1969, Secretary of State Rogers presented a plan for an Israel-Egypt settlement

options.label: Reject the plan and escalate: take the war across the Canal instead of relying on the Bar-Lev line and air raids
options.advocate: Ezer Weizman, then chief of operations (S601)

lasting.label: Arms industry and US aid after the war

cite.quote: General Weizman argued for renewal of all-out war against Egypt

forks.title: Answering the Black Panthers
forks.text: Young Mizrahi protesters from Jerusalem's poor neighbourhoods are demanding equality, housing and schooling.

options.label: Meet the leaders and expand welfare programmes
options.advocate: Prime Minister Golda Meir's government

lasting.label: Lighter fiscal drag than a large plan

options.note: The protests put poverty and ethnic inequality on the agenda (S273).

options.label: A national neighbourhood-renewal and schooling plan
options.advocate: The Black Panthers protest movement

cite.quote: In a series of mass demonstrations in 1971, the Panthers demanded social services and an end to economic inequality and discrimination.

forks.title: Yom Kippur morning: strike first?
forks.text: Intelligence on the morning of 6 October indicates Egypt and Syria will attack that evening. Chief of Staff Elazar wants a full mobilisation and a pre-emptive air strike; Defence Minister Dayan prefers a narrower call-up. Prime Minister Meir must decide within hours.

options.label: Order a large-scale reserve call-up but no pre-emptive strike
options.advocate: Prime Minister Meir

lasting.label: Israel not seen as the aggressor
Arab armies strike first; heavy opening losses
Loss of faith in the leadership after the surprise

options.note: Meir approved a large mobilisation but refused a pre-emptive strike; the US airlift began on 12 October (S209, S1306).

options.label: Full mobilisation and a pre-emptive air strike on Syria
options.advocate: Chief of Staff Elazar (S1307)

lasting.label: Syrian air defences and batteries hit first

cite.quote: It was not until 5 a.m. on October 6 that Elazar first recommended a full, immediate mobilization of forces and a preemptive air strike.

options.label: Call up only the air force and two armoured divisions
options.advocate: Defence Minister Dayan (S1307)

lasting.label: Too few reserves on the lines
Reservists and employers spared a mass call-up
The country feels unprepared and unprotected

cite.quote: I propose mobilizing all the Air Force reserves, an armored division in the Golan Heights and a division in the Sinai.

forks.title: After the Agranat interim report
forks.text: The Agranat Commission's interim report of 1 April 1974 recommends dismissing the intelligence chief and others and finds the Chief of Staff responsible, but declines to rule on the ministers. Public protest demands more.

options.label: Accept the findings on the officers; the government resigns
options.advocate: Prime Minister Meir

lasting.label: Anger that ministers were not judged
A culture of accountability takes root

options.note: Meir's government resigned about ten days later; Rabin formed a government on 3 June 1974 (S236, S1352, S1299).

options.label: Dismiss the officers named; keep Meir and Dayan in office
options.advocate: Defence Minister Dayan, who refused to resign under pressure (S600)

lasting.label: Continuity of the economic and defence team
Continuity for the US-brokered disengagement talks

cite.quote: Dayan said only last week that he would not resign from the caretaker government under pressure from his critics because that would be tantamount to confessing responsibility

options.label: Extend accountability to the ministers and remove Dayan too
options.advocate: Capt. Motti Ashkenazi's protest, backed by several Labor MKs (S600)

lasting.label: Responsibility seen to reach the political level

cite.quote: a one-man campaign for his ouster conducted by a Yom Kippur War veteran, Capt. Mordechai Ashkenazi, outside the Prime Ministers Office last week

forks.title: Sebastia: the Gush Emunim settlers
forks.text: Gush Emunim's Elon Moreh group has tried eight times to settle at the old Sebastia railway station in northern Samaria and has been removed by the army seven times. The government must settle the confrontation.

options.label: Compromise: allow about 25 families into the Kadum army camp
options.advocate: Defence Minister Peres, brokering; Prime Minister Rabin approved after hesitation (S1237, S1238)

lasting.label: Government seen to yield to pressure
Settlement in the West Bank criticised

options.note: About 25 families moved into the Kadum camp (later Kedumim) in December 1975 (S239).

options.label: Keep evicting the settlers; no new settlement in northern Samaria
options.advocate: Prime Minister Rabin's initial position (S1237)

lasting.label: Law applied evenly, welcomed by the secular public

cite.quote: Rabin opposed Jewish settlement in centers of Arab population

options.label: Authorise settlement throughout the West Bank
options.advocate: Gush Emunim; Peres reportedly supported its demands (S239, S1238)

cite.quote: Peres, who arranged the compromise, has made no secret of his support of the Gush demands for free Jewish settlement on the West Bank.

forks.title: Entebbe: negotiate or rescue?
forks.text: Air France Flight 139 has been hijacked to Entebbe, Uganda. The hijackers separate Israelis and Jews from other passengers and demand the release of prisoners. The cabinet is split between talks and a long-range raid.

options.label: Approve the rescue raid
options.advocate: The cabinet that approved the raid on 3 July (S1378)

lasting.label: Admired abroad, criticised at the UN for violating Ugandan sovereignty
Pride and belief in the state's reach

options.note: On the night of 3-4 July commandos freed the hostages (102 by JTA's count at the time, 103 by Britannica's); three hostages and the unit commander, Lt. Col. Yonatan Netanyahu, were killed, as were all seven hijackers and 20 to 45 Ugandan soldiers (sources differ), and Dora Bloch was later murdered in Uganda (S1378, S1379, S5303, S5305).

options.label: Negotiate a prisoner release
options.advocate: The Rabin government, which publicly kept negotiating with the hijackers (S1380)

lasting.label: No raid on a sovereign state; goodwill kept in Africa
Resources kept for the civilian economy
Hijacking seen to pay; public humiliation
Confidence in the state's reach shaken

cite.quote: Israeli officials publicly maintained that they were continuing to negotiate with the hijackers

forks.title: Camp David: the Sinai settlements
forks.text: Egypt will sign a peace treaty only with full withdrawal from Sinai, including the settlements around Yamit that Israel built in the Rafah salient. Prime Minister Begin has to say what he will do about them.

options.label: Agree to let the Knesset decide on evacuating the Sinai settlements
options.advocate: Prime Minister Begin

lasting.label: Peace dividend: lower defence burden, Sinai oil, US aid
Yamit trauma for the settler camp and the right

options.note: The Knesset approved the evacuation; Yamit was evacuated from 23 April 1982 and most buildings in the Sinai settlements demolished (S254).

options.label: Insist on keeping the Rafah-salient settlements such as Yamit
options.advocate: Begin's opening position (S1375)

lasting.label: No peace dividend; larger defence burden
Settler camp and its supporters kept on side
Sinai oil fields and farms kept three more years

cite.quote: Begin insisted on an agreement over Sinai in which the parties would continue negotiating for a final peace treaty and after three months, if they were successful then he would submit the question of withdrawing the settlements to the Knesset.

options.label: Leave the settlements in place under UN or Egyptian administration
options.advocate: Begin's 'My Plan for Peace' (S1239)

lasting.label: Settlers keep their homes for now
Settler camp and the right not betrayed
Egypt unlikely to accept; front stays tense
Seen as a way to avoid full withdrawal

cite.quote: In our peace proposal we suggested that a second, narrow United Nations zone be created in the northern Sinai around the district of Yamit

forks.title: Iraq's Osirak reactor
forks.text: Iraq's French-built Osirak (Tammuz) reactor near Baghdad is close to completion. The cabinet is divided over striking it, relying on covert action and diplomacy with France, or postponing the decision.

options.label: Approve an air strike on the reactor
options.advocate: Prime Minister Begin (S1423)

lasting.label: Security Council condemnation and US displeasure
Strained French and US trade ties

options.note: Eight F-16s destroyed the reactor on 7 June 1981, killing ten Iraqi soldiers and a French engineer; the Security Council condemned the attack (S1491, S1422).

options.label: Rely on covert sabotage and diplomacy with France
options.advocate: Labor leader Shimon Peres, who urged Begin not to order the strike (S1423)

lasting.label: No attack on a state's reactor
Reactor completed under French fuel and supervision
French trade and arms contracts preserved
Public fear of an Iraqi bomb

cite.quote: the new government in France should be given a chance to change its policy of selling nuclear material to Iraq

options.label: Postpone until clearer evidence shows the reactor is near hot
options.advocate: Gur, who argued the reactor was further from completion (S1423)

lasting.label: Restraint; no attack on a state's reactor
French and European science ties kept
Anxiety as the strike window closes

cite.quote: According to Gur, he had information that indicated that the nuclear reactor near Baghdad was not as close to completion as Begin had suggested.

forks.title: How far into Lebanon?
forks.text: The government is preparing a large operation against PLO bases in Lebanon after repeated cross-border fire. The cabinet will approve a limited zone, but Defence Minister Sharon has larger aims in mind.

options.label: Advance up to Beirut, fighting Syrian forces, to remove the PLO and back a Christian-led government
options.advocate: Defence Minister Sharon (S1234)

lasting.label: Siege of Beirut and civilian deaths condemned
Lebanon trauma and the peace movement

options.note: The war expanded beyond the 40 km aim; the IDF fought Syria and besieged West Beirut, and over 14,000 PLO fighters left in August-September (S1424, S1393).

options.label: Limit the operation to a 40 km zone and halt there
options.advocate: The cabinet that approved the 40 km aim (S1234, S1424)

lasting.label: A narrower, more widely supported war
PLO and Syrian forces remain beyond the zone
Rocket threat to the north only partly lifted
A consensus war the public accepts

cite.quote: The Israeli Cabinet thought it was approving an incursion 40 kilometers north of its border.

options.label: Postpone any invasion; wait for a clearer provocation and diplomacy
options.advocate: The large cabinet minority and the Labor opposition that held up the May 1982 plan (S602)

lasting.label: Northern towns lose residents under fire

cite.quote: the large minority within the Cabinet opposed to it and the refusal by the Labor Party opposition to give it their backing

forks.title: The Kahan Commission's findings
forks.text: The Kahan Commission found that Lebanese Phalangist militiamen killed hundreds of Palestinian and Lebanese civilians in Sabra and Shatila after the IDF let them in. It holds Israel indirectly responsible and finds Defence Minister Sharon personally responsible for disregarding the danger.

options.label: Accept the report; Sharon leaves the Defence Ministry but stays in the cabinet
options.advocate: Prime Minister Begin and the cabinet that voted 16-1 (S1960)

lasting.label: Commission findings become a norm of accountability

options.note: The cabinet voted 16-1 to accept the report, with Sharon the lone dissenter; he left Defence and stayed as minister without portfolio (S1960, S257).

options.label: Reject the personal findings and keep Sharon at Defence
options.advocate: Defence Minister Sharon, who cast the only vote against (S1960)

lasting.label: Findings of a judicial inquiry set aside
Seen to reject its own commission
Likud base and coalition kept together

cite.quote: Defense Minister Ariel Sharon, whose resignation was called for by the commission, cast the lone dissenting vote.

options.label: Accept the report and remove Sharon from the government
options.advocate: The Tel Aviv rally of September 1982 (Peace Now, Alignment), which demanded Begin's and Sharon's resignations (S1954)

lasting.label: Loss of the architect of the Lebanon campaign
Likud base alienated; coalition near collapse
Right-wing distrust of the courts and commissions

cite.quote: Rallying in a plaza before City Hall here, the throng gave thunderous roars of applause and cheers to speakers who called on Mr. Begin and his Defense Minister, Ariel Sharon, to resign.

forks.title: Ending triple-digit inflation
forks.text: Inflation ran at about 445% in 1984 and the unity government must stop it. Options range from a sharp shock to continued negotiated package deals or tying the shekel to the dollar.

options.label: Devalue, freeze prices and wages by agreement with the Histadrut, cut the budget and stop printing money
options.advocate: The unity government with the Histadrut (S1403, S1404)

lasting.label: Stable macro climate lets the economy grow
Social cost borne by weaker groups

options.note: The plan combined devaluation, budget cuts and temporary price controls; inflation fell to about 20% within about two years (S1403, S1406).

options.label: Continue negotiated wage-price package deals with the Histadrut instead of a cabinet-imposed plan
options.advocate: Histadrut Secretary-General Kessar, who blasted the cabinet for acting without prior negotiation with the Histadrut (S1403)

lasting.label: Jobs and housing for growing families
Unstable prices deter R&D and high-tech

cite.quote: He blasted the Cabinet for agreeing to them without prior negotiations or consultations with Histadrut.

options.label: Link the shekel exclusively to the dollar
options.advocate: Former Finance Minister Aridor's 1983 plan (S1407)

lasting.label: Exports squeezed by an overvalued currency
Wages tied to a hard peg
Export towns hit by an overvalued currency

cite.quote: a plan he had just announced that would link Israel's faltering currency exclusively to the U.S. Dollar

forks.title: Syrian tanks in Jordan
forks.text: Syrian armour has crossed into northern Jordan to back the Palestinian fighters against King Hussein. Washington is coordinating with Jerusalem, and Hussein has asked for outside help. Israel's response is the player's call; the Syrian withdrawal follows within days either way.

options.label: Mass troops on the Golan, fly over the Syrian columns and coordinate with Washington, but do not attack
options.advocate: Prime Minister Meir's cabinet, with Ambassador Rabin in Washington

cite.quote: sending troops to the border with Syria and fighter planes over Syrian tanks in Jordan
was opposed in principle to diversionary move if it was not aimed ultimately at source of problem

lasting.label: Seen as a reliable partner by Washington
A friendly Hashemite buffer survives on the eastern border
Reserves held on the Golan border

options.note: Israel moved troops to the Syrian border and flew over the Syrian tanks in Jordan without attacking; Jordan's army and the threat of intervention ended the incursion (S765).

options.label: Strike the Syrian armour in Jordan from the air at Hussein's request
options.advocate: King Hussein, who asked for outside intervention (relayed by Kissinger)

cite.quote: I request immediate physical intervention both air and land
would look favorably upon an Israeli air attack

lasting.label: Syrian armour broken; lessons on joint air operations
Israeli planes in an Arab state's civil war
Hussein tainted as rescued by Israel; the east front stays brittle
Sustained air operations and risk of wider war

options.label: Prepare a ground move into Syria to draw off the invaders
options.advocate: US Assistant Secretary Sisco, who asked Rabin to query Jerusalem

cite.quote: Pursuant to Sisco's request, Rabin agreed to query Jerusalem re alternative option calling for Israeli move into Syria

lasting.label: US trade, aid and arms flow deepens
Casualties and fear of a wider war with Iraq and Egypt
Forces stretched across Golan and the canal

forks.title: The Sinai interim agreement
forks.text: After Kissinger's shuttle diplomacy, Egypt and Israel have a second interim accord on the table: an Israeli pullback in Sinai, with US monitors and indemnification, and no Egyptian peace declaration. The Knesset must vote.

options.label: Sign the interim agreement and withdraw to the new line
options.advocate: Prime Minister Rabin and Defence Minister Peres

cite.quote: Defense Minister Shimon Peres, argued forcefully in favor of the agreement
by a vote of 70-43 with seven abstentions

lasting.label: Seen as flexible; US relations repaired
Sinai front thinned out; war seen as less likely
Gush Emunim and the right protest
Depth lost; reliance on early-warning stations

options.note: The Knesset approved the agreement on 4 September 1975 by 70 votes to 43 with seven abstentions (S767).

options.label: Reject the interim agreement and hold the Sinai passes and oil fields
options.advocate: Rimalt of the Likud Liberals, joined by Dayan, Ben Porat and Hadar from Labor

cite.quote: Elimelech Rimalt, leader of the Liberal Party wing of the opposition Likud; voted against the agreement. He contended that Egypt gave no quid pro quo for Israeli concessions

lasting.label: Passes and depth in Sinai kept
Sinai oil kept, no indemnification bill
US technology and research ties cool

forks.title: Sadat's offer to come to Jerusalem
forks.text: President Sadat has said he is ready to travel to Jerusalem. Prime Minister Begin must decide whether to issue the invitation through the Americans now. The Chief of Staff has warned that the offer could cover war preparations.

options.label: Invite Sadat to address the Knesset at once
options.advocate: Prime Minister Begin; the Knesset approved with only Rakah abstaining

cite.quote: Only the three-member Rakah Communist faction abstained in the vote.
Perhaps this is the beginning of the Arab awakening

lasting.label: A belief that peace is possible
Settler camp and the right anxious about what follows
Guard lowered on the southern front

options.note: The Knesset approved the invitation on 16 November 1977 and Sadat addressed it on 21 November (S768).

options.label: Delay the invitation until Egypt's intentions are verified and keep the army on alert
options.advocate: Chief of Staff Gur

cite.quote: war materiel mobilized against Libya could be turned against Israel

The Knesset appeared unperturbed by a warning by Chief of Staff Gen. Mordechai Gur, published in Yediot Achronot today, that Sadat's offer to visit Israel may be a smokescreen to cover Egyptian preparations for war.

lasting.label: A habit of verifying intentions; army kept alert
Seen as stalling on a peace offer

forks.title: The Koenig memorandum
forks.text: A confidential memorandum by the Interior Ministry's Galilee commissioner, Israel Koenig, has been published. It proposes harsh measures against Israeli Arabs in the Galilee. Ministers disagree about what to do with it.

options.label: Shelve it quietly as a civil servant's internal letter
options.advocate: Prime Minister Rabin, Foreign Minister Allon and Interior Minister Burg

cite.quote: He praised Interior Minister Yosef Burg for quietly shelving it

lasting.label: No official endorsement of the memorandum
Suspicion between Arab and Jewish citizens

options.note: Rabin refused to put the memorandum on the cabinet agenda; Allon denounced it and praised Burg for shelving it (S769).

options.label: Debate it in cabinet and formally repudiate it
options.advocate: Tourism Minister Kol and Health Minister Shemtov

cite.quote: Tourism Minister Moshe Kol of the Independent Liberal Party and Health Minister Victor Shemtov of Mapam

lasting.label: The state seen to reject discrimination

options.label: Adopt Koenig's recommendations as policy for the Galilee
options.advocate: Likud and the religious parties, who praised Koenig's ideas

cite.quote: drew praise from Likud quarters and from the religious parties

lasting.label: New Jewish communities in the Galilee grow
Denser Jewish presence along the northern border
Arab citizens treated as a threat
Seen to discriminate against its Arab citizens

forks.title: The Golan Heights
forks.text: Syria has shown no sign of talking. Begin's cabinet has agreed to apply Israeli law to the Golan Heights; the opposition objects. Is the Golan to be brought under Israeli law, kept as it is, or joined by a wider annexation?

options.label: Apply Israeli law, jurisdiction and administration to the Golan Heights
options.advocate: Prime Minister Begin

cite.quote: Should we wait for years, possibly for five generations, for the Syrians to change their minds?

lasting.label: Golan headwaters under permanent Israeli control
Settlement and tourism on the Golan

options.note: The Knesset passed the law on 14 December 1981, with Israeli law applying to the Golan from that day (S770).

options.label: Keep the Golan under military administration and leave its status for talks
options.advocate: The Labor Alignment opposition

cite.quote: Despite opposition from the Labor Alignment, the bill is expected to pass the required three readings today

lasting.label: Seen to leave room for diplomacy
Druze not forced to choose their status
Long-term water control on the Golan stays unsettled

options.label: Drop the Golan bill and move to annex the West Bank instead
options.advocate: Geula Cohen of Tehiya

cite.quote: Cohen said today that in view of the Cabinet's decision she would withdraw her Golan bill and present, instead, a motion for the immediate annexation of the occupied West Bank.

lasting.label: Settlement surges in Judea and Samaria
Mountain aquifer under permanent Israeli control

forks.title: Forming a government after the 1984 election
forks.text: The July 1984 election left neither bloc able to govern alone. Labor and Likud are bargaining over policy and over who becomes prime minister. A broad coalition is one path; a narrow Labor-led government is another.

options.label: A seven-party national unity government with Peres and Shamir rotating as premier after 25 months
options.advocate: Shimon Peres and Yitzhak Shamir

cite.quote: Shamir will replace Peres as Premier, and Peres will replace Shamir as Deputy Premier and Foreign Minister

lasting.label: Broad cover for the stabilisation programme
Paralysis on peace policy and settlements

options.note: The unity government was presented to the Knesset after 40 days of negotiation, with the premiership to rotate after 25 months (S772).

options.label: A narrow Labor-led coalition without Likud
options.advocate: Labor Alignment sources

cite.quote: Some Labor sources let it be known over the weekend that the Alignment was prepared to form a narrow-based coalition government if talks with Likud continued to be stalled.

lasting.label: A government free to invite Jordan to talks
The deficit is not cut in time

forks.title: The 1977 economic upheaval
forks.text: Finance Minister Simcha Ehrlich has drafted, in secret since June, a plan to end currency controls, float the pound and cut subsidies. The Likud government stays in office either way; the cabinet decides how far and how fast to go, and who is cushioned.

options.label: Float the pound, lift currency controls and cut subsidies at once
options.advocate: Finance Minister Simcha Ehrlich and Premier Begin

cite.quote: The first move was to establish a free-floating currency.
Finance Minister Simcha Ehrlich defended his economic policies in the Knesset today

options.note: The cabinet approved the plan on Friday 28 October 1977 with one vote against and one abstention. The pound lost 48 percent that year and a wave of wildcat strikes followed (S5020, S5021).

lasting.label: Currency controls lifted and capital drawn back
Float and subsidy cuts push prices up
Price shock falls on low-income towns

options.label: Float the pound but compensate low-income families in full
options.advocate: Absorption Minister David Levi

cite.quote: Absorption Minister David Levi told the Jewish Telegraphic Agency today that he voted against the Ehrlich plan because it failed to provide adequate compensation for the poor.

lasting.label: Poorer towns cushioned from the shock

options.label: Keep the controls and the crawling peg; pay cost-of-living allowances in advance
options.advocate: Histadrut Secretary General Yeruham Meshel

cite.quote: Meshel said this morning that Histadrut will demand advanced payment of cost-of-living allowances

lasting.label: Multiple exchange rates and controls stay

forks.title: Autonomy talks: Israel's guidelines
forks.text: Under the Camp David framework Israel and Egypt open talks at Beersheba on autonomy for the West Bank and Gaza. The cabinet decides what its negotiating team carries to the table.

options.label: Adopt Begin's 20-point plan as guidelines, keeping control of public land and a sovereignty claim after five years
options.advocate: Premier Begin

cite.quote: The plan that emerged from the Cabinet today consisted of 20 points instead of the original 22 submitted by Begin.

options.note: The cabinet adopted the plan as guidelines, not as a formal position. Dayan resigned in October 1979 over the autonomy policy (S5023, S5024).

lasting.label: Talks stall over land and sovereignty
Public-land policy keeps West Bank settlement open

options.label: Offer a short, flexible opening position that leaves land and sovereignty open
options.advocate: Defense Minister Ezer Weizman, with Foreign Minister Dayan and Deputy Premier Yadin

cite.quote: strongly stated by Defense Minister Ezer Weizman last week that the autonomy plan was too hardline and too detailed to serve even as an opening position

lasting.label: Talks keep Egypt and Washington engaged
Likud right and settlers see concessions

options.label: Set autonomy aside and pursue a territorial compromise with Jordan
options.advocate: Labor Party (Abba Eban)

cite.quote: Dayan also rejected the Labor Party’s territorial compromise approach based on a settlement with Jordan
He quoted former Foreign Minister Abba Eban as saying it was "offering something we don't have to someone who doesn't want it."

lasting.label: Talks over territory reach Palestinian towns
Coalition strain with the Likud camp

forks.title: After the Elon Moreh ruling
forks.text: On 22 October 1979 the Supreme Court ordered the Gush Emunim settlement of Elon Moreh removed from expropriated Arab land and gave the settlers 30 days. The ruling stands; the cabinet decides how to respond.

options.label: Accept the ruling and move the settlers to a State-owned site
options.advocate: Premier Begin and Housing Minister David Levy

cite.quote: Housing Minister David Levy of Herut spoke forcefully for standing up to the Gush
the settlers of Elon Moreh have agreed to leave voluntarily and accept an alternative site offered by the government at Djebel Kebir

options.note: On 6 December 1979 the settlers agreed to leave voluntarily for Djebel Kebir, about six miles away; government policy was to settle only on State-owned land (S5027).

lasting.label: Relocation and compensation for the settlers

options.label: Legislate to cancel the ruling and keep Elon Moreh and the seized land
options.advocate: Agriculture Minister Ariel Sharon and the Gush Emunim

cite.quote: Agriculture Minister Ariel Sharon and Education Minister Zevulun Hammer dissented sharply from Begin
The Agriculture Minister was apparently voicing the demands of the Gush Emunim for legislation that would retroactively nullify the Supreme Court

lasting.label: More West Bank settlement on private land
Private Arab land open to seizure

options.label: Move the settlers to State land but keep the seized site for military installations
options.advocate: Education Minister Zevulun Hammer (National Religious Party)

cite.quote: Hammer, a leader of the National Religious Party, met with Begin later to present an NRP plan that would shift the Elon Moreh settlers to State-owned land

lasting.label: Land not returned to its owners

forks.title: Defence budget against inflation
forks.text: After April 1980 inflation of 10.2 percent Finance Minister Yigal Hurwitz froze the national budget. The Defence Ministry says cuts endanger projects such as the Lavi fighter. The cabinet decides how deep the defence cut goes.

options.label: Cut IL 7 billion from the defence budget
options.advocate: Premier Begin's cabinet

cite.quote: The Cabinet agreed to slice IL 7 billion (about $150 million) from the Defense Ministry

options.note: After a nine-hour session ending on 20 June 1980 the cabinet cut IL 7 billion; Hurwitz had demanded 15 billion. Hurwitz resigned on 11 January 1981 (S5029, S5039).

lasting.label: Aircraft and defence R&D programmes kept

options.label: Cut IL 15 billion from the defence budget
options.advocate: Finance Minister Yigal Hurwitz

cite.quote: Hurwitz had demanded on IL 15 billion ($320 million) cut which he insisted was the only way to halt the soaring inflation rate

options.label: Hold defence at its present level and find savings elsewhere
options.advocate: Defense Minister Ezer Weizman

cite.quote: Defense Minister Ezer Weizman declared that he would resign if

forks.title: The Jerusalem Basic Law
forks.text: Geula Cohen's private bill would proclaim united Jerusalem Israel's capital in a Basic Law. Egypt has suspended the autonomy talks and the government is reportedly reluctant. The cabinet and coalition decide how the bill is handled.

options.label: Pass the Basic Law: Jerusalem, Capital of Israel
options.advocate: Geula Cohen (Tehiya) and the National Religious Party

cite.quote: was proposed last month by Geula Cohen of the ultranationalist Tehiya faction, as a private member
by a vote of 69-15 with three abstentions, thus incorporating it into Israel

options.note: The Knesset passed the law 69-15 at the end of July 1980. The Security Council censured it 14-0, with the US abstaining, and called for the removal of the 11 embassies in Jerusalem (S5032, S5033).

lasting.label: UN censure and embassies leave Jerusalem

options.label: Let the bill wait in the Knesset queue and keep the autonomy talks open
options.advocate: Begin government (reported eager to bury the bill)

cite.quote: The government is reportedly eager to bury the bill.
reports from Cairo said Premier Menachem Begin had given oblique assurances to Sadat that the bill would be buried in committee

lasting.label: Embassies stay and Egypt stays at the table
Tehiya and NRP charge doubt over Jerusalem

options.label: Pass the law with funding, a Jerusalem authority and holy-places guarantees written in
options.advocate: Mayor Teddy Kollek and the Labor Alignment

cite.quote: The Alignment insisted on introducing as many as possible practical proposals into the text of the bill, most of them suggested by Jerusalem Mayor Teddy Kollek

forks.title: The bank shares collapse
forks.text: Bank shares fell sharply as the public sold them to buy dollars before a devaluation, and the stock exchange is closed. Tens of thousands of investors stand to lose heavily. The new Shamir cabinet decides whether the State stands behind the shares.

options.label: Link the bank shares to the dollar with a state guarantee
options.advocate: MK Avraham Shapiro (Agudat Israel, Bank of Israel advisory board)

cite.quote: They yielded to the arguments of Aguda Israel MK Avraham Shapiro, chairman of the Bank of Israel
Agreement was reached to link bank shares to the U.S. Dollar, in effect a government guarantee of their value.

options.note: The cabinet backed the shares in the early hours of 11 October 1983; economists estimated 140 billion shekels. A commission under Justice Beisky later recommended that the Bank of Israel governor and the heads of the five largest banks resign (S5034, S5036).

lasting.label: Savers protected; confidence in the banks

options.label: Refuse a state guarantee and let the shares find their price
options.advocate: Finance Minister Yoram Aridor

cite.quote: The decision was taken despite strenuous opposition by Finance Minister Yoram Aridor

lasting.label: Savers lose; trust in the banks shaken
Banks forced to stop propping up their own shares

forks.title: Leaving Lebanon
forks.text: The IDF has been in Lebanon since 1982 and the Nakura talks are stalled. The Defence Ministry proposes a unilateral withdrawal in three stages over six to nine months, which splits the unity cabinet. The cabinet decides.

options.label: Withdraw in three stages, with or without an agreement
options.advocate: Premier Peres and Defense Minister Rabin

cite.quote: which is strongly favored by Premier Shimon Peres and by Rabin

options.note: The first stage (Awali and Sidon) was completed on 16 February 1985 and the cabinet began the second on 4 March (S5038).

options.label: Oppose a unilateral pullout; hold a 30-km security zone until a security agreement
options.advocate: Ariel Sharon and Moshe Arens

cite.quote: It was strongly opposed by former Defense Minister Moshe Arens of Likud
Sharon reportedly urged that the IDF establish a 30-kilometer deep security zone north of the Israeli border

forks.title: Slowing the economy: the Sapir programme
forks.text: Exports lag, the trade deficit and prices are rising, and about 24,000 workers are already jobless (45,000 projected by January 1967). Finance Minister Sapir proposes a three-year stabilisation programme that accepts temporary unemployment; coalition partners and the Histadrut are split over who should carry the burden.

options.label: Adopt Sapir's three-year programme: freeze wages and prices, cut cost-of-living allowances, push exports
options.advocate: Finance Minister Pinhas Sapir
options.note: The cabinet adopted the programme on 12 September 1966, with three abstentions (Mapam's Bentov and Barzilai, and the NRP's Shapira); unemployment rose through 1967 until the post-war boom (S5126).

cite.quote: Mr. Sapir has been the principal architect of the new economic plan which was adopted by the Cabinet last night

options.label: Adopt the programme but add a compulsory loan and higher taxes on middle and higher incomes
options.advocate: Mapam, with Achdut Avodah in agreement

lasting.label: Wage earners and weaker towns protected
Slower export restructuring and heavier tax drag

cite.quote: Mapam holds that the Sapir plan bears too heavily on the wage earners.

options.label: Put joblessness first: public works, slum clearance and housing for young couples
options.advocate: The Tel Aviv secretariat of Mapai and Mayor Mordechai Namir

lasting.label: Building workers and new households helped

cite.quote: The Tel Aviv secretariat of Mapai urged immediate Government action to curb unemployment in the building trades in Tel Aviv.

forks.title: Sadat's Canal offer
forks.text: President Sadat offers to reopen the Suez Canal if Israel pulls back from its east bank, and ties any further ceasefire extension to a withdrawal timetable. The Canal has been shut since 1967 and the Bar-Lev line is under strain. Ministers differ on how far to go.

options.label: Answer with questions and a conditional offer: a limited pullback only against an end to belligerency, with no Egyptian troops in the vacated zone
options.advocate: Prime Minister Meir's inner circle: Allon, Eban, Dayan and Galili

lasting.label: Bar-Lev line and Canal positions kept
Seen to offer too little for the Canal
Cabinet kept together on a middle line

options.note: Israel offered a conditional pullback but no deal was reached in 1971; the Canal stayed closed until after the 1973 war (S5128).

cite.quote: consists of Deputy Premier Yigal Allon, Foreign Minister Abba Eban, Defense Minister Moshe Dayan and Minister-Without-Portfolio Israel Galili
Israel will agree to a reopening of the Suez Canal if Egypt will declare and end to her belligerency against Israel

options.label: Take Sadat's offer up in earnest: negotiate a Canal reopening with a partial withdrawal and no ruling out a timetable
options.advocate: Chaim Tzadok, chairman of the Knesset Defence and Foreign Affairs Committee

lasting.label: Israel seen to meet Egypt halfway
A reopened Canal and calmer front lower the defence burden
Forces thinned along the Canal bank
Hawks and Gahal oppose any retreat
Part of the public distrusts a pullback without peace

cite.quote: Chaim Tzadok, declared today that President Sadat
should not be rejected out of hand.

options.label: Reject any pullback; offer a joint commission to reopen the Canal with guaranteed access for Israeli ships
options.advocate: Opposition leader Menachem Beigin (Herut)

lasting.label: Hawks and the Herut base satisfied
Canal and Red Sea trade stay closed
Public reassured the Canal line is held

cite.quote: Opposition leader Menachem Beigin demanded last night that a canal reopening be discussed separately from questions of withdrawal, territory or refugees.

forks.title: The US initiative and the unity government
forks.text: Washington asks Israel to accept a 90-day ceasefire and talks under UN Resolution 242 to end the War of Attrition. Gahal, with six of 24 ministries, says it will leave the unity government formed on the eve of the Six-Day War if the cabinet accepts.

options.label: Accept the US initiative and ceasefire; Gahal leaves the cabinet
options.advocate: Prime Minister Meir, Deputy Premier Allon and Foreign Minister Eban

lasting.label: Israel seen to take the US initiative
US arms and aid pledges kept
Unity government ends; Herut in opposition

options.note: The cabinet accepted; Gahal voted 117-112 to quit on 5 August, the Knesset backed the government 66-28, and the ceasefire began on 7-8 August (S5130, S5131).

cite.quote: Deputy Premier Yigal Allon and Foreign Minister Abba Eban staunchly defended the government

options.label: Reject the initiative and keep the national unity government
options.advocate: Menachem Beigin and Herut

lasting.label: Seen to block a US peace effort
US arms and aid at risk
Continued war burden and a cooler West

cite.quote: Menachem Beigin, the 56-year-old co-founder and leader of Herut. said his opposition to the U.S. Initiative was not exaggerated

forks.title: How deep into south Lebanon
forks.text: After the coastal road massacre, the army enters south Lebanon to clear PLO bases. The first plan was a belt about six miles deep. Ministers must decide how far to go and when to leave; tens of thousands of Lebanese civilians are fleeing north and the Egyptian talks hang in the balance.

options.label: Widen the operation to a belt up to the Litani and hold it until an arrangement keeps the PLO out
options.advocate: Prime Minister Begin, Defence Minister Weizman and Chief of Staff Gur

lasting.label: PLO rocket bases pushed back from the border
Northern towns shielded by a buffer zone
Civilian casualties and refugees in Lebanon
Public debate over widening the operation
Cost of the operation and the zone

options.note: The army held a belt about 10 km deep; Resolution 425 created UNIFIL and Israel withdrew in June 1978, leaving positions to Maj. Haddad's militia (S5133).

cite.quote: was effectively concluded with Israeli forces in control of a 100-kilometer security belt along the Lebanese border of an average depth of 10 kilometers

options.label: Keep to the original six-mile belt and withdraw early to protect the Egyptian track
options.advocate: MKs Amnon Rubinstein, Meir Talmi and Yossi Sarid; Defence Minister Weizman favoured early withdrawal

lasting.label: Rocket threat returns to the border
Northern towns fear the return of rockets

cite.quote: Amnon Rubinstein, of the Democratic Movement for Change, Meir Talmi of Mapam, Yossi Sarid of the Labor Party and others blamed Israel
favors an early withdrawal of Israeli forces from south Lebanon

forks.title: Ratifying the treaty with Egypt
forks.text: The draft peace treaty with Egypt reaches the cabinet and Knesset. Supporters point to ending the southern front; opponents in Likud and the NRP object to leaving Sinai and to the treaty's link to a wider settlement. Sinai's Israeli settlers and the Palestinians of the territories are both affected.

options.label: Ratify the treaty as drafted
options.advocate: Prime Minister Begin

lasting.label: US aid package for the withdrawal
Autonomy talks promised under the framework
Settler camp and nationalist right break with the government

options.note: The cabinet approved on 11 March and the Knesset voted 95-18 on 22 March 1979 (S5135).

cite.quote: The Knesset overwhelmingly approved the Israeli-Egyptian peace treaty by a 95-18 majority

options.label: Reject the treaty and keep the Sinai airbases, oil fields and settlements
options.advocate: Likud dissenters Geula Cohen, Yigael Hurwitz and Moshe Arens, and NRP MKs including Haim Druckman

lasting.label: Settler camp and nationalist right satisfied
Seen to walk away from peace
US aid and arms goodwill withheld

cite.quote: Geula Cohen, Yigal Cohen Orgad; Yigal Cohen, Yigael Hurwitz; Moshe Shamir; Yosef Rom; and Moshe Arens, the chairman of the Knesset

options.label: Ratify only after loosening the preamble's link to a wider settlement
options.advocate: Yehuda Ben-Meir, chairman of the NRP Knesset faction

lasting.label: National-religious camp kept in the coalition
Treaty signed, but the US and Egypt irked by the delay
Delay puts the aid timetable at risk

cite.quote: Yehuda Ben-Meir, chairman of the National Religious Party (NRP) Knesset faction
if the Cabinet failed to demand a revision of that clause in the preamble, he would oppose the draft and urge his party to do the same

forks.title: Syrian missiles in the Bekaa
forks.text: After Israeli aircraft shot down two Syrian helicopters near Zahle on 28 April, Syria deployed SAM-6 missiles in Lebanon's Bekaa valley. Israel has threatened to destroy them; the US envoy Philip Habib is shuttling between capitals with a package. Northern towns are under rocket threat from PLO bases.

options.label: Give Habib's mediation time while continuing strikes on PLO bases
options.advocate: Prime Minister Begin's government

lasting.label: US ties kept; Washington's mediation honoured
Resolve shown without a Syrian war

options.note: Begin gave Habib 'ample time'; the missiles stayed in the Bekaa and the crisis was still unresolved a year later (S5137).

cite.quote: said after a two hour meeting with U.S. special envoy Philip Habib this morning that he would give the American diplomat

options.label: Destroy the SAM batteries by air attack unless Syria removes them
options.advocate: Prime Minister Begin, in his June 1981 statement

lasting.label: Syrian missile umbrella removed from the Bekaa
Washington and Cairo angered by a new front
Fear of war with Syria in an election year
Escalation costs and a cooler US
Northern towns exposed to Syrian retaliation

cite.quote: "I merely said in Netanya that we insist that Mr. Habib undertook the mission to get the Syrian missiles out of Lebanon. If he does not get them out we shall see to it that they get out," Begin told reporters today.

options.label: Accept the US package: curtail operational flights over Lebanon in exchange for a return to the pre-April status quo
options.advocate: US special envoy Philip Habib

lasting.label: Israel seen to take the US package
Closer US economic and trade ties
Fewer air operations; missiles and PLO bases stay
Christian allies and northern towns feel abandoned
Likud base angry at a concession

cite.quote: U.S. special envoy Philip Habib left for Damascus today, reportedly with a proposed American package to resolve the crisis between Israel and Syria

forks.title: Inquiring into Sabra and Shatila
forks.text: Lebanese Christian forces allied with Israel have killed at least 300 Palestinian civilians in the Sabra and Shatila camps in west Beirut. President Navon and the opposition call for an independent inquiry; Prime Minister Begin is reluctant, and the cabinet has so far taken no decision.

options.label: Set up a judicial commission of inquiry with broad terms of reference
options.advocate: Prime Minister Begin, after a week's reversal, and the unanimous cabinet

lasting.label: Israel seen to examine its own conduct
Inquiry acknowledges the harm to Palestinians
Government shaken by the findings ahead

options.note: After the cabinet refused on 21 September, it voted unanimously on 28 September to set up a judicial commission; Justice Kahan chaired it (S5141, S5142).

cite.quote: Begin himself proposed the judicial commission and it was then unanimously approved

options.label: Hold no official inquiry; defend the army and the government
options.advocate: Prime Minister Begin (his position to 28 September)

cite.quote: Premier Menachem Begin who strongly opposed an official inquiry on grounds that it would be an admission of Israeli guilt for the blood bath

options.label: Set up the inquiry and have the Prime Minister and Defence Minister step aside pending its findings
options.advocate: The Labor Alignment leadership

lasting.label: Responsibility seen to reach the top
Israel seen to hold itself to account
Government crisis during the Lebanon war

cite.quote: Labor Alignment leaders continued to demand the resignation of Begin and Sharon

forks.title: Ikrit and Baram: return or compensation
forks.text: The residents of Ikrit and Baram, two Christian Arab villages near the Lebanese border evacuated in 1948 and later razed, petition to return. The army holds that the security grounds remain and the cabinet fears a precedent for other evacuated villages; the villagers and their supporters call it a matter of justice. The petition is before the cabinet.

options.label: Keep the area closed on security grounds and compensate and rehouse the villagers
options.advocate: Prime Minister Meir and the cabinet majority, on the army's security advice

cite.quote: The Cabinet ruled by a majority decision today not to permit the former residents of Ikrit and Baram villages to return

options.note: On 23 July 1972 the cabinet voted by a majority not to let the villagers return, and offered compensation and relocation instead (S5426).

lasting.label: Compensation and new housing for the villagers
Public protest by writers and Mapam

options.label: Let the villagers return to the village sites and rebuild
options.advocate: Deputy Premier Allon, Minister Kol and the two Mapam ministers, with Archbishop Joseph Raya

cite.quote: voted against that decision, along with Deputy Premier Yigal Allon and Tourism Minister Moshe Kol
The Greek Catholic Archbishop, Joseph Raya, pursuing his effort to persuade

lasting.label: The state seen to keep its 1948 promise
Seen to act on a question of justice
Civilians back on the exposed border
Fear of claims from 20 other evacuated villages

forks.title: Answering the Soviet diploma tax
forks.text: On 3 August the USSR set large exit charges on emigrants with higher education, aimed at Jewish scientists and graduates. Soviet Jews keep arriving only as fast as Moscow lets them go. Israel, the Jewish Agency and the Americans disagree on how loudly to answer.

options.label: Take the issue to the Knesset, the UN General Assembly, UNESCO and world opinion
options.advocate: Prime Minister Meir and Foreign Minister Eban
options.note: The Knesset unanimously demanded repeal on 24 August, and Eban told the cabinet he would raise the charges at the UN General Assembly and UNESCO (S5428, S5429).

lasting.label: Soviet Jewry's cause taken up abroad

options.label: Leave the pressure to quiet US-Soviet diplomacy and avoid a public confrontation
options.advocate: US State Department officials, including Assistant Secretary Joseph Sisco

cite.quote: American officials prefer quiet diplomacy to bring pressure on the Soviets
It was indicated that Joseph Sisco, the US Assistant Secretary of State briefed Ambassador Yitzhak Rabin on US plans to combat the higher exit charges.

lasting.label: Goodwill in Washington on aid and arms

options.label: Back the linking of US trade benefits to free emigration
options.advocate: Senators Henry Jackson and Jacob Javits

cite.quote: would withhold most favored nation status from any country that denies its citizens the right to emigrate
Sen. Jacob K. Javits, a leading supporter of the Jackson legislation

lasting.label: Linkage opens the door to a mass exodus
Backed by a bipartisan Congress majority
Friction with the administration's detente policy

forks.title: Answering Munich
forks.text: Eleven members of Israel's Olympic team were killed after the Munich Games attack of 5 September. The cabinet had decided beforehand not to negotiate with the terrorists. The Knesset must now decide how Israel acts against those behind it.

options.label: Act against the terrorist organizations, with strikes on their bases and a covert Mossad campaign against those behind Munich
options.advocate: Prime Minister Meir and her adviser on terrorism, Aharon Yariv
options.note: The Knesset resolved to act with perseverance against the terrorist organizations; Yariv later confirmed that the government approved the killing of 10 to 15 Black September figures (S5431, S5433).

lasting.label: Public sense that Munich was answered
Operations in friendly countries and a wrongful killing in Norway
Arab citizens uneasy at the campaign

options.label: Lead with a diplomatic drive for European action against terrorism and tighter protection of Israelis abroad
options.advocate: Foreign Minister Eban

cite.quote: Foreign Minister Abba Eban indicated to the Cabinet today that Israel was making a major diplomatic effort to get European governments to step up their measures against terrorist activities within their borders.

lasting.label: Seen to answer through law and diplomacy
Costly protection of Israelis and missions abroad
Planners of Munich left at large
Public anger at a restrained answer

options.label: Legislate the death penalty for convicted terrorists
options.advocate: Menachem Begin (Gahal), Yizhar Harari (Alignment) and Gideon Hausner (Independent Liberals)

cite.quote: Yizhar Harari of the Alignment and Gideon Hausner of the Independent Liberals both made a strong plea for the death penalty

lasting.label: Demand for a harsh answer met
Arab citizens fear a two-tier justice system

forks.title: The Galili document
forks.text: Before the autumn election, Labor leaders draw up a settlement and territories platform drafted by Minister Israel Galili from proposals by Defence Minister Dayan. It would lift the ban on private land purchases in the territories and build settlements in Rafiah and the city of Yamit. Mapam and part of Labor object. The platform is yours to shape.

options.label: Adopt the Dayan-Galili plan: lift the land purchase ban and settle Rafiah and Yamit
options.advocate: Defence Minister Dayan, Minister Galili and Prime Minister Meir
options.note: The Labor Secretariat approved the plan 78-0 on 4 September 1973 for the party's election platform (S5435).

lasting.label: Buffer zone between Gaza and Sinai
Settlement of the territories criticised abroad
Land purchases in the territories alienate Arab residents
Mapam and Labor doves split from the platform

options.label: Keep the ban on private land purchases and limit settlement to state-planned sites
options.advocate: Finance Minister Sapir, with Mapam and the Labor doves

cite.quote: Finance Minister Pinhas Sapir is known to be opposed to parts of it

lasting.label: Territories policy kept open for a settlement
Land in the territories not opened to purchase

options.label: Adopt the Rafiah and Yamit settlement plan but defer land purchases for further discussion
options.advocate: Moshe Carmel, former Transport Minister

cite.quote: a suggestion by former Transport Minister Moshe Carmel that the question of land purchases in the territories undergo further discussion

lasting.label: State-led settlement in Rafiah and Yamit
Buffer zone between Gaza and Sinai
